status: public discovery candidates; all conclusions remain synthesis/inference unless independently established
purpose: Seed the House with non-obvious, source-grounded syntheses that demonstrate rare value rather than generic reference accumulation.

candidates.title: A Garden does not merely help. It leaves people more able to act.
candidates.question: What separates a genuinely generative institution from one that produces good outputs while preserving dependency?

A.claim: Autonomy, competence and relatedness support higher-quality motivation and development.

B.claim: The relevant bridge is whether support becomes internalized skill, agency and relational security rather than permanent external control.

C.claim: Capabilities concern real opportunities to achieve valued functionings, while robust commons institutions depend on workable participant-grounded rules and capacities.

candidates.synthesis: A project-Garden can be evaluated by whether it increases independent future capability: people gain skill, voice, real options, durable relations and the ability to function without indefinite dependence on the Gardener.
candidates.novelty: This turns Garden from a harmony metaphor into a capability-production test for schools, NGOs, welfare systems, communities, platforms and institutions.
test: Does participation increase competence over time?
Can participants make meaningful choices and exit?
Do material conversion factors improve, or are only resources distributed?
Can the system keep functioning when central support withdraws?
Does governance incorporate participant knowledge and feedback?
disconfirmers: Outputs improve but autonomy/competence/capability do not.
The system's success depends on permanent gatekeeper control.
Exit, criticism or adaptation materially reduce access to basic capability.
candidates.confidence: strong synthesis; project terminology remains interpretive

candidates.title: Mission drift can be seen as a Spirit–Mind–Body divergence.
candidates.question: How can an institution preserve its mission statement while becoming a different institution in practice?

A.claim: Research describes organizations facing competing institutional logics and stakeholder pressures that can reshape mission-oriented action or gradually reorient practice.

B.claim: Mission can remain stable in declared purpose while decision criteria, reporting systems, incentives, funding or capacity shift.

C.field: Inhabited House Spirit / Mind / Body projection
C.claim: Spirit captures mission/legitimacy, Mind captures decision and information systems, Body captures material capacity, funding and infrastructure.

candidates.synthesis: Purpose drift becomes observable when Spirit, Mind and Body stop reinforcing one another: the stated mission says one thing, internal metrics/governance optimize another, and money/assets/constraints reward a third.
candidates.novelty: This suggests a practical mission-drift audit that compares words, decisions and resource flows instead of treating mission as a single statement.
test: Compare founding/current mission language over time.
Compare board/management KPIs and actual decision criteria.
Map funding/revenue concentration and contractual constraints.
Compare beneficiary/participant experience with public purpose.
Trace whether adaptation changes the 'how' while preserving the 'why', or changes the 'why' itself.
disconfirmers: Observed operational change is consistent with mission-preserving adaptation.
Funding/governance changes do not alter prioritization or outcomes.
Apparent divergence disappears when time, legal duties or crisis context are included.
candidates.confidence: promising synthesis; requires entity-specific longitudinal evidence

candidates.title: Source authority is a relationship to be tested, not a badge to inherit.
candidates.question: How should the archive decide whether a source deserves trust without reducing credibility to official status or popularity?

A.claim: Research argues that people evaluate communicated information through plausibility, source competence, source benevolence/intentions and argument quality.

B.claim: A source may be highly competent but conflicted, benevolent but uninformed, official but stale, or independent but methodologically weak.

C.field: Project Eye / Source Authority / Information Ecology
C.claim: The House already separates provenance, evidence class, contradiction, freshness and interpretive layers.

candidates.synthesis: The Eye should score or describe source trust dimensionally: competence for this claim, access to evidence, incentives/conflicts, methodological transparency, freshness, corroboration and argument quality.
candidates.novelty: This can turn the archive's source layer into a trust graph rather than a source hierarchy, especially when institutions disagree.
test: What direct access does the source have to the claim?
What expertise is relevant to this exact claim?
What incentives or constraints could bias reporting?
Which independent sources corroborate or contradict it?
disconfirmers: The dimensions add complexity without improving prediction/correction.
Trust descriptions become covert ideological ratings.
The archive cannot separate claim-specific authority from institution-wide reputation.
